full_judgment:
2. The Appeal and Arbitration Committee of the Board, by its decision dated 28-9-2004, resolved to reinstate him (Annexure-D to the Writ Petition No. 8860 of 2005) with a liberty to take action against him, in case of recurrence of similar incidents of misconduct. 

 10. In the present case, the contemner No. 2 ignored the directions of this Court in spite of his knowledge from the letter dated 28-2-2006 of the Board. 

 The school is run, managed and administered by the Managing Committee consisting of 11 members including the Chairman and this deponent as Head-master is only one of the members. As he has no power to appoint, suspend, dismiss or remove any teacher, he has no power to reinstate any teacher who has been proposed to be dismissed by the meeting of the Managing Committee and, as such, if the order of this Hon'ble Court is to be implemented, in that case, it is respectfully submitted that the entire Managing Committee through its Chairman needs to be directed to implement the decision." 

 29. Mr ABM Nurul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the contemner No. 2, submits that the present petitioner was suspended because of some misconduct. Subsequently, his suspension order was withdrawn by the Appeal and Arbitration Committee of the Board but the contemner No. 2 was not alone responsible to implement the order of this Court. He submits that now the present petitioner has already been reinstated in his post and withdrew his outstanding wages. 

 36. Having considered the facts and circumstances of the case and foregoing narrative, we are of the view that the contemner Nos. 2 and 5 committed contempt of this Court. We find that pursuant to the order dated 27-9-2007, the petitioner had already been reinstated in his post. So, in our view, justice should be met, if we take a lenient view in awarding punishment to the above contemners.
